newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down slightly against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down slightly at 8.2958 on Monday from 8.2956 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, with no impact seen from the increase in China's trade surplus, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2955.
At the weekend, China posted a trade surplus of $3.8 billion in the first two months of 1997, compared with a deficit of $439 million for the same period last year.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2958 and moved below 8.2960 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2869 and a low of 8.2962.
Trading was more active than last Friday with most done at 8.2958, traders said.
Dealers said the increase in the trade surplus had no immediate or direct impact on the market since it had been expected.
"The yuan was pushed to an intraday high suddenly by speculative buying," one dealer said. "Such an action may make trading a little more active but has no impact on the yuan's trend."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to consolidate around 8.2960 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at 6.7003 from 6.7150 against 100 Japanese and down at 1.0719 from 1.0710 against the Hong Kong dollar.
